# Tree-based structures (Octree, Pointer Tree, Sparse Voxel DAG)

Also called: Sparse Voxel Trees, Hierarchical Sparse Volumes

## Overview
Tree-based structures organize sparse volumetric data into a hierarchical graph where internal nodes define spatial subdivisions and leaf nodes store voxel values [G]. This family solves the memory inefficiency of dense grids by omitting empty space and the traversal overhead of flat sparse lists by leveraging spatial locality [G]. They differ from sibling structures like [Hash Grids](936-hash-grids.md) by providing explicit spatial hierarchy for culling, and from [Brick-based Hierarchical Storage](2793-brick-based-hierarchical-storage.md) by operating on individual voxel granularity rather than fixed-size blocks [G].

## Shared principles
All structures in this family share the following mechanism:
1. **Recursive Subdivision:** The 3D domain is recursively divided into sub-volumes [G]. In standard octrees, each node has 8 children [G]. In pointer trees, the branching factor $N$ varies ($N^3$ children) [G].
2. **Sparsity Encoding:** Empty regions are represented by null pointers or absence of children, rather than storing zero-valued voxels [G]. This provides compression proportional to the sparsity of the data [G].
3. **Hierarchical Traversal:** Rendering or access requires traversing from the root to the leaf [G]. This allows skipping large empty volumes (culling) and adapting resolution to view distance or detail requirements [G].
4. **Spatial Locality:** Children of a node are spatially contiguous [G]. This locality is often exploited via Morton ordering (Z-order curve) to map 3D coordinates to 1D keys, enabling efficient neighbor lookups and linear array representations in implicit variants [G].

## Subtopics

### [Compact pointer tree](844-compact-pointer-tree.md)
Uses variable branching factors ($N^3$) and 8-bit relative offsets for compact storage. Choose when memory footprint is critical and data has high redundancy.

### [Sparse Voxel DAGs](2791-sparse-voxel-dags.md)
Merges identical subtrees into a Directed Acyclic Graph to eliminate topological redundancy. Choose when the volume contains repeated geometric patterns.

### [Octree-based structures](2792-octree-based-structures.md)
Fixed 8-way branching with implicit or explicit storage. Choose for standard spatial indexing and neighbor queries.

### [Span Space Tree](4379-span-space-tree.md)
Refines interval trees to manage scene complexity for large volumes. Choose for complex scene culling.

### [Sparse Voxel Tree (SVO Tree)](4983-sparse-voxel-tree-svo-tree.md)
Standard sparse voxel octree implementation. Choose for general-purpose ray marching.
